text:
alice: FYI customer AcmeHealth on Private is hitting intermittent API failures after a config change. 503s and TLS handshake timeouts to control-plane endpoints. Ticket #5489.

bryan: any error examples? logs?

alice: From their side they see: \"x509: certificate is valid for private.redwood.internal, not control.redwood.ai\" and repeated: \"dial tcp 34.210.12.45:443: i/o timeout\". Also kube-dns showing NXDOMAIN for control.redwood.ai sometimes.

sara: that smells like networkpolicy/CNI egress blocking + DNS caching flipping. Did they recently enable a default-deny egress policy in the redwood namespace?

alice: They did a lockdown last night. They said \"default-deny egress\" applied to namespace and then added allow rules for S3 and KMS only.

bryan: can we get their NetworkPolicy? quick check: \n```
kubectl -n redwood get networkpolicy -o yaml
kubectl -n redwood describe pod redwood-controller-0
```

alice: they pasted a snippet: \n```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
```
No egress rules beyond that + serviceAccount rule for s3 kms.

sara: aha. default deny egress blocks DNS (UDP 53) and HTTPS to our control plane (control.redwood.ai -> 34.210.12.45). Even if they allow FQDNs for S3 via an egress proxy, kube-dns and TLS to our endpoints must be allowed. Also some CNIs (Calico) enforce IP-based rules so FQDN rules won't match.

alice: customer ran `curl -v https://control.redwood.ai:443` from a pod and it hangs. `kubectl exec` tcpdump shows SYNs but no reply.

bryan: likely their egress policy doesn't include UDP/53 to kube-dns or UDP/53/TCP/53 to 10.100.0.10. Also need to allow egress to our IPs and to the CA endpoint for cert validation if they pin internal CAs.

sara: suggested quick repro steps for them:
1) `kubectl -n redwood apply -f - <<EOF` add a permissive test policy that allows egress to DNS + control plane
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-dns-and-controlplane-test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.0/12  # kube-dns cluster IP range
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 34.210.12.45/32  # control.redwood.ai
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
EOF
```
2) `kubectl exec -n redwood -it redwood-controller-0 -- curl -v https://control.redwood.ai:443` verify.

alice: they applied and `curl` worked immediately. TLS handshake completed and API calls resumed.

bryan: good. long-term advise: prefer serviceAccount-based networkpolicies or allow egress to our published IP ranges/CIDRs rather than FQDN. Also explicitly allow access to kube-dns and CRD/webhook endpoints. If using Calico, you can use GlobalNetworkPolicy to allow egress from the node to the control plane health ports.

sara: also note some environments have egress allowlists on the firewall; we gave them our egress IPs: 34.210.12.45, 52.14.200.10, and 3.18.66.2 (all TCP/443). If their CNI blocks ephemeral outbound ports, healthcheck connections fail — suggest allowing ephemeral ports 1024-65535 for outbound to those IPs.

alice: they rolled a fix: updated policies to allow DNS + our IPs and opened ephemeral ports. Monitoring shows requests normalized. Customer happy.

infra-bot: Incident resolved: set networkpolicy exemptions for control plane and dns (ticket 5489).

deploy-bot: Noted: recommend adding a KB article template for Private customers about networkpolicy egress rules.
